sections.title: Countries & territories
sections.description: All political features on the map. Capitals from the reference snapshot; Natural Earth population estimates; the reference year appears below each figure. A dash means no capital is recorded in the source.

rows.name: Nauru
rows.capital: Yaren (seat of government; no official capital)

sections.title: Cities
sections.description: National capitals, selected first-level subdivision capitals, and cities with a source population of at least one million. First-level capitals are included for Russia, China, India, USA, Brazil, Canada and Mexico, including shared and seasonal seats. Natural Earth estimates use differing urban definitions and reference dates; these are not current census counts.

rows.name: Daman
capitalOf: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

rows.name: Krasnogorsk
rows.note: Seat of Moscow Oblast government; the oblast has no official capital.

sections.title: Rivers & canals
sections.description: One row per river or canal, including locally named river reaches. Canal endpoints are terminals, not a direction of flow. Lengths are approximate reference values; headwater conventions vary. Countries include border reaches, not every country in the drainage basin.

rows.name: Suez Canal
rows.story: An artificial sea-level waterway connecting the Mediterranean and Red Sea through Egypt. Opened in 1869, it lets ships travel between Europe and Asia without rounding Africa.

sections.title: Lakes
sections.description: Reference surface areas and volumes, not live water levels. Available measurement years appear below the figures. A dash means the measurement is not recorded; the Aral Sea is listed as its North and South remnants.

rows.name: Gatun Lake
rows.story: An artificial lake created for the Panama Canal, providing its elevated navigable crossing and water for the locks.

rows.name: Lake Nasser
rows.story: The Aswan High Dam reservoir flooded part of historical Nubia and prompted the rescue of monuments including Abu Simbel. Its Sudanese reach is known as Lake Nubia.

sections.title: Mountain ranges
sections.description: Mapped span is the approximate area of the generalized Natural Earth or curated footprint, rounded to 1,000 km²—not a precise geological boundary. Countries describe conventional range extents.

rows.name: Bismarck Range
rows.story: Part of New Guinea’s central highlands, the range includes Mount Wilhelm, Papua New Guinea’s highest summit. It is on the mainland, separate from the Bismarck Archipelago.

rows.name: Dolomites
rows.story: Dolomite rock towers preserve ancient tropical marine environments, now uplifted into the Alps. This is a generalized range footprint, not the UNESCO property boundary.

sections.title: Peaks
sections.description: Selected summits, including the ten highest independent peaks and China’s Five Yue, with elevations in metres above sea level. Border peaks list both countries; territorial claims are described on the map.

rows.name: Mont Blanc
rows.story: The Alps’ highest summit lies in a disputed Franco-Italian border sector. Elevation shown is the 2023 snow-cap survey (4805.59 m); snow and ice heights vary.

rows.name: Mount Elbert
rows.story: The Sawatch Range summit is the highest point of the Rocky Mountains.

rows.name: Mount Elbrus
rows.story: A twin-summit volcano, conventionally Europe’s highest mountain when the continental boundary follows the Greater Caucasus watershed.

rows.name: Mount Heng (Hunan)
rows.story: Southern mountain of the Five Yue, a sacred geography of imperial rites and pilgrimage.

rows.name: Mount Heng (Shanxi)
rows.story: Northern mountain of the Five Yue, a sacred geography of imperial rites and pilgrimage.

rows.name: Mount Hua
rows.story: Western mountain of the Five Yue, a sacred geography of imperial rites and pilgrimage.

rows.name: Mount McKinley (Denali)
rows.story: North America’s highest summit; Denali is its longstanding Alaska Native name. The US federal name returned to Mount McKinley in 2025.

rows.name: Mount Rainier
rows.story: A glacier-clad active volcano shapes the landscape and volcanic hazards of the Pacific Northwest.

rows.name: Mount Song
rows.story: Central mountain of the Five Yue, a sacred geography of imperial rites and pilgrimage. The point marks Liantian Feng, the Song massif’s highest summit, rather than lower Junji Feng.

rows.name: Mount Tai
rows.story: Eastern mountain of the Five Yue, a sacred geography of imperial rites and pilgrimage.

rows.name: Mount Whitney
rows.story: The highest summit in the contiguous United States rises above the Owens Valley.

sections.title: The five oceans
sections.description: The five named basins of one connected global ocean.

rows.name: Arctic Ocean
rows.setting: Around the North Pole, north of Eurasia and North America

rows.name: Atlantic Ocean
rows.setting: Between the Americas and Europe & Africa

rows.name: Pacific Ocean
rows.setting: Between Asia & Oceania and the Americas

rows.name: Southern Ocean
rows.setting: Encircling Antarctica; conventionally south of 60° S

sections.title: Seas & coastal waters
sections.description: Named seas, bays, gulfs, straits and other marine features already on the map. Part of shows the immediate containing water body. Ocean associations include indirect connections; transitional waters list more than one ocean.

rows.name: Bight of Benin
rows.story: The lagoon-backed coast between Cape Saint Paul and Cape Formoso links the ports of Lomé, Cotonou and Lagos along the northern Gulf of Guinea.

rows.name: Bight of Bonny
rows.story: Also known as the Bight of Biafra, this eastern Gulf of Guinea embayment extends from the Niger Delta to Cape Lopez, with the volcanic island of Bioko offshore.

rows.name: Burgas Bay
rows.story: A sheltered western Black Sea embayment on which Burgas developed as a major Bulgarian port.

rows.name: Corisco Bay
rows.story: An island-studded coastal bay between Cabo San Juan and Cap Esterias, where estuaries open into the eastern Gulf of Guinea.

rows.name: Dnieper-Bug Estuary
rows.story: The Dnieper and Southern Bug meet in a two-armed liman, linked to the Black Sea through the narrow entrance beside Kinburn Spit.

rows.name: Garabogazköl Basin
rows.story: Also known as Kara-Bogaz-Gol, this shallow hypersaline lagoon receives water from the Caspian Sea through a narrow inlet. Strong evaporation concentrates its salts, making the basin an important evaporative sink for the Caspian.

rows.name: Gulf of Aqaba
rows.story: A deep northeastern arm of the Red Sea, shared by four countries and connected to the main basin through the Straits of Tiran.

rows.name: Gulf of Lion
rows.story: The Mediterranean embayment along Occitanie and Provence includes the Rhône delta and the French continental shelf.

rows.name: Gulf of Odessa
rows.story: Also called the Gulf of Odesa, this coastal indentation frames the city and its Black Sea port.

rows.name: Gulf of Saint-Malo
rows.story: Also called the Norman–Breton Gulf, this island-studded part of the English Channel lies between northern Brittany and the Cotentin peninsula. Strong tides shape its bays, estuaries and island passages.

rows.name: Gulf of Suez
rows.story: The northwestern arm of the Red Sea leads to the Suez Canal, linking this rift-bounded gulf to a global shipping route.

rows.name: Gulf of Taranto
rows.story: The Ionian Sea reaches between Calabria and the Salento peninsula here. Taranto, founded as a Greek colony, developed into an important commercial and naval port at the head of the gulf.

rows.name: Kalamita Bay
rows.story: A broad western Crimean bay south of Yevpatoria, bounded by the Yevpatoria and Lukull capes. Crimea is internationally recognized as Ukrainian territory and is controlled by Russia.

rows.name: Karkinit Bay
rows.story: Between mainland Ukraine and northwestern Crimea, the bay includes internationally recognized coastal wetlands. Crimea is internationally recognized as Ukrainian territory and is controlled by Russia.

rows.name: Palk Strait
rows.story: Shallow waters between India and Sri Lanka, mapped together with adjoining Palk Bay; Adam’s Bridge separates them from the Gulf of Mannar and their shoals constrain navigation.

rows.name: Taganrog Bay
rows.story: The shallow northeastern arm of the Sea of Azov receives the Don River and forms the maritime approach to Taganrog and the lower Don.

rows.name: Taman Bay
rows.story: A shallow, island-studded embayment between the Chushka and Tuzla spits on the eastern side of Kerch Strait.

rows.name: Türkmenbaşy Gulf
rows.story: Also called Krasnovodsk Bay, this shallow Caspian embayment supports migratory waterbirds and the port of Türkmenbaşy.
